title: setup-wizard: drive pi/opencode/kimi agent CLIs, reject unknown choices
description: Stage 2 only detected claude/codex/kimi and stage 6 only automated claude/codex; entering pi (or any unknown CLI) fell through to the '*' branch and silently skipped the README rewrite while still printing '✓ Setup complete'. Added pi/opencode detection, automated delegation for pi (-p), opencode (run), kimi (--print -p), a validation loop on the agent choice, and a loud warning for unrecognized CLIs. Also listed supported CLIs in scaffold README requirements.
notes: Follow-up redesign: stage 6 no longer trusts the agent's exit status. run_agent output streams to the terminal and is captured to a log; completion is verified by the hard check from AGENT-SETUP.md (README.md no longer mentions setup-wizard.sh). On failure or a lying exit-0 run the wizard reports the tail of the agent output and loops back to agent re-selection; giving up requires explicit confirmation and is recorded loudly in the closing summary. Stage 7 warns before deleting .scaffold/ when the rewrite is still undone. Verified with two stubbed end-to-end scenarios (lie-then-retry-succeeds, fail-then-give-up).
close_reason: Implemented in scaffold/setup-wizard.sh and scaffold/README.md on main; core branch picks it up via GitHub Actions rebuild

title: Ignore Beads JSONL export on core branch
description: Update the core branch .gitignore so .beads/issues.jsonl remains an untracked passive export. Record the core build policy that builds must run through GitHub Actions rather than directly/local builds.
close_reason: Updated core branch .gitignore and recorded the GitHub Actions-only core build policy in project memory.

title: README: 대표 scaffold Usage 워크플로우 추가
description: main 브랜치 README에 bunx degit으로 core scaffold를 내려받고 setup-wizard.sh를 실행한 뒤 새 에이전트 세션에서 mattpocock skills setup까지 마치는 대표 Usage 흐름을 문서화한다.

title: core scaffold: wizard-driven bootstrap (setup-wizard.sh)
description: The bootstrap is driven by an interactive bash wizard at the scaffold root (setup-wizard.sh, authored in the mattpocock-skills wizard template format), not by handing the whole procedure to an agent. Rationale: 6 of 7 bootstrap steps are deterministic shell (verify, git init, bd init --skip-agents, bd setup codex, plugin install, ADR bead) — an agent adds latency and nondeterminism, and the agent-driven run needed bypassPermissions. The wizard detects installed-and-logged-in harness CLIs (claude auth status, codex login status), runs the mechanical steps itself, then invokes the chosen agent for the generative rest (README rewrite, acceptEdits suffices). The wizard removes .scaffold/ and itself at the end. AGENT-SETUP.md now contains only the agent tasks.

title: core scaffold: skills via Claude plugin marketplace install, not vendoring
description: Supersedes the HANDOFF's vendoring design (.agents/skills tree + .claude/skills symlink + sources.json pinned SHAs). mattpocock/skills is now registered in the official Claude plugin marketplace, so standard installation is simpler and stays updated. Bootstrap installs mattpocock-skills and ponytail at project scope (claude plugin install --scope project), which records them in .claude/settings.json. Consequences: no vendored skill tree, no symlink, no sources.json; scaffold shrinks to instruction files + docs + .scaffold bootstrap kit.

title: core scaffold: no provenance of ajchemist/agent-ready-alpha in scaffold output
description: The core branch tree must contain no reference to 'ajchemist', 'agent-ready-alpha', or the degit source repo. Rationale: degit consumers start a fresh unrelated project; upstream identity is noise and leaks template origin. Enforcement: create-core-branch.sh greps the generated tree and fails the build on any match (sources.json pins upstream skill repos only, which are third-party, not this repo).

title: core scaffold: README.md lifecycle — onboarding doc pre-setup, rewritten to project README by the bootstrap agent
description: The scaffold ships a README.md that documents only how to onboard (run the agent against .scaffold/AGENT-SETUP.md). AGENT-SETUP.md instructs the agent to replace README.md with a real project README (title, description) as part of bootstrap, since the agent performs onboarding anyway. AGENT-SETUP.md itself is written as an agent-optimized instruction/skill document: imperative steps, documented defaults, no questions.

title: core scaffold: bootstrap deletes .scaffold/ at the end
description: HANDOFF originally said .scaffold/ may be left for the user to delete. Decision: AGENT-SETUP.md's final step removes .scaffold/ itself, so a bootstrapped project carries no scaffold residue. Rationale: .scaffold/ is bootstrap-only tooling (AGENT-SETUP.md, sources.json, manifest.json, verify.sh); leaving it invites drift and confuses later agents.
